THAT ATTEMPT FAILED and the failure is logged rather than hidden: this source is authoritative but publishes a DIFFERENT BASIS, so it cannot set ATTOM-basis bands. ⚠️⚠️ THE THIRD BASIS — DO NOT MIX: "percent of residential LOANS in foreclosure inventory" (MBA / LPS-Black Knight / FL-EDR) is a STOCK of loans in process denominated in MORTGAGES; ATTOM's rate is a FLOW of filings denominated in HOUSING UNITS. They differ by roughly an order of magnitude and are NOT convertible. FL at 3.73% of loans (Nov-2014) sits in the same era as ATTOM-basis annual rates in the low single digits. HEURISTIC: a FL foreclosure number near 3-4% is almost certainly the LOANS basis, not the housing-units basis. This is now the THIRD distinct basis documented for this one concept (annual / H1-cumulative / quarterly / monthly on ATTOM, plus loans-inventory on MBA) — the single largest source of false comparison in this domain. ★ WHAT THE PULL DID YIELD, and it is genuinely useful: (1) FL was #1 by BOTH count and rate in CY2014, extending the documented FL #1 streak backwards; (2) ★ TIMELINE ANCHOR corroborating the conversion-phase thesis — FL took 946 days to foreclose in 2014-Q4 (vs 169 days at the start of 2007) against a NATIONAL average of 604 days, and ATTOM H1-2026 puts the national average at 563 days, LOWER than the 2014 national figure. So the "conversion accelerating / timelines at lowest-since-2013" read is corroborated against an independent 2014 primary, not just internally. (3) FL judicial-foreclosure state (1 of 22 per MBA) = structurally slower pipeline, which is WHY FL accumulates a visible backlog and why FL level vs speed must be read separately. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BANDS: Orange (>1.00%) and Red (>1.50%) remain JUDGMENT PLACEHOLDERS, explicitly graded as such in CLAUDE.md; the 0.63%-to-5.56% interval is UNMAPPED. Re-anchor when a 2012-13 annual FL rate on the ATTOM housing-units basis surfaces.
